source.title: Improving Generalization of Complex Models under Unbounded Loss Using PAC-Bayes Bounds
source.authors: Xi-Tong Zhang; Avrajit Ghosh; Guang-Da Liu; Rongrong Wang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures training and test accuracy gaps during its own PAC-Bayes and ERM training experiments, using ResNet18 on CIFAR10. It compares a different training procedure and does not test the claim's central random-label memorization result.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported training/test accuracy gaps and directly reported training or test accuracy effects of the study's training procedure. Mentioned optimizer and regularization results from cited work are not rows. The paper reports that Stage 1 training loss exceeds testing loss, but provides no numerical values for that comparison; the gap plot is figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study's SGD, Adam and AdamW baseline comparisons directly bear on V4 through test accuracy; training accuracy is not required to establish its held-out-performance comparison. The tuning includes weight decay and noise injection, extending beyond V4's limited-tuning setting. No magnitude-aware sharpness ranking is measured, and the batch-size comparisons do not establish a fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their new bound and training framework improve practical PAC-Bayes training and approximately match optimally tuned ERM test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains stochastic Gaussian posterior and prior distributions by minimizing a PAC-Bayes objective, with an optional noise-injection refinement stage, and compares with tuned ERM baselines. It does not use random-label memorization tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with architecture, dataset, prior type, batch size, learning rate, warmup duration, γ settings, training stage, and augmentation; the study describes PAC-Bayes performance as relatively robust to several of these choices.

fits_no_version.finding: PAC-Bayes training has a smaller training-test accuracy gap and less sensitivity to hyperparameter variation in the reported comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For ResNet18 on CIFAR10, the proposed PAC-Bayes training reduces the observed generalization gap and its sensitivity to hyperparameters relative to ERM.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed method achieves competitive accuracy and exhibits varying sensitivity to learning rate, batch size, warmup, bound parameters and training stages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed PAC-Bayes procedure approximately matches tuned ERM across the evaluated tasks, with robustness to several hyperparameter choices.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report training loss above testing loss during Stage 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reported PAC-Bayes Stage 1 analysis shows training loss exceeding testing loss.

record.problems: The central claim versions about random-label memorization, width, architecture comparisons, adaptive optimizer generalization, dropout, sharpness measures, and memorized-example removal are not tested. Several relevant performance summaries are test accuracy only, so they do not measure train-test error gaps. Figure 4 provides no tabulated gap values. CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 test data were used to select baseline hyperparameters, which the authors say may slightly inflate baseline performance. The augmentation experiment uses an ad-hoc effective sample size.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each Table 2 model-dataset-method accuracy cell: these cells are test-accuracy-only comparisons and do not report the training-error behavior required by the versions. Rows for GNN and GLUE test-accuracy tables are omitted because they do not bear on any listed version or add a distinct train-test gap measurement. Figures 5–10 and other plot-only training details were omitted where the text supplied no specific numeric outcome relevant to a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy compared with natural-label training under the same recipe.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The restriction to tuning only learning rates and decay schedules; corresponding training performance; switching optimizers during training; word-level language modeling.
Batch-size effects with verified equal epoch budgets and controlled adaptations to the training recipe.
An isolated dropout comparison and its dataset-size or augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, correlation with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Its optimizer comparisons test V4 even though the paper primarily evaluates its own method. Baseline hyperparameters were selected using CIFAR test data, which can inflate reported performance; uncertainty is not supplied for these CNN comparisons. The grouped R3 and R4 rows require splitting into model-dataset-optimizer comparisons. Theoretical discussion of flatness and learned posterior noise does not test V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level test accuracy with random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under limited tuning; Adam and SGD rows compare test accuracies but do not report corresponding training performance.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets versus small batches; the paper reports batch-size comparisons but does not state a fixed epoch-budget comparison.
Dropout effects on held-out error and its interaction with dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons to norm- or margin-based measures. The paper discusses sharpness and PAC-Bayes posterior noise but does not report the version's measure.
Removing memorized examples and comparing the effect with random example removal.

AdamW exceeds SGD for VGG13 on CIFAR100, 61.0% versus 60.1%; AdamW falls below SGD in the other three settings. Baseline tuning includes momentum, learning rate, weight decay and noise injection; baseline hyperparameters are selected using test accuracy.
statements.problem: For this study, the Adam–SGD reversal between batches 128 and 2048 is correct, but AdamW does not remain below SGD in every setting. The broader tuning supports a scope qualification rather than a challenge within V4's limited-tuning condition.
